info.title: pingtxt API
info.summary: REST API of the pingtxt hub.
info.description:
Everything the web UI does goes through this API.

## Authentication

Create a personal token in **settings → api tokens** and send it as a bearer token:

```
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer ptk_..." https://status.example.com/api/monitors
```

- **read** tokens can call every `GET` endpoint marked *read*.
- **write** tokens can also create, change and delete. Only admins can create them.
- Account and instance settings (users, tokens, 2FA, settings, backups) need a browser session: tokens get `403`.

## Native apps (OAuth 2.1)

Apps sign the user in with OAuth 2.1, authorization code + PKCE (S256), through the hub's own login page (password, 2FA, single sign-on), and get a bearer access token (`pma_...`) that works on the whole API like a token above.

- The iOS app is the built-in public client `pingtxt-ios` with redirect URI `pingtxt://oauth` (no secret, no registration). Other clients register with `POST /oauth/register`.
- Scopes: `read` or `write`. `write` is granted only to admins; viewers always get `read`. The scope the user picked is in the token response.
- Access tokens last 1 hour. Refresh tokens last 30 days from their last use and rotate at every refresh: keep only the newest one. Presenting an already used refresh token revokes the sign-in.
- Sign out with `POST /oauth/revoke`. Users see and disconnect apps in **settings → api tokens → connected apps**.
- Metadata: `/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server` (RFC 8414) and `/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/api` (RFC 9728).

## Roles

Admins can change everything. **Viewers** are read-only: every request that is not `GET` answers `403`, and secrets in monitors and notification channels are replaced by `********`.

## Conventions

- Bodies are JSON (`Content-Type: application/json`); other content types on writes get `415`.
- Times are Unix milliseconds. Ids are integers.
- Errors are `{"error": "message"}` with a 4xx/5xx status.
- Browser requests from another origin are refused (`403`).

AI assistants can use the same API through the MCP server on `/mcp`.

post.summary: Subscribe to a status page by email
post.description:
Sends a confirmation link to the address; nothing else is sent until it is confirmed. The answer is the same for new, waiting and already confirmed addresses. On a custom domain the path is `/api/public/status/subscribe`. Limited to 10 requests per client address and 3 per email address every 15 minutes.

**Access:** No authentication.

post.summary: Unlock a password protected status page
post.description:
Checks the page password and sets a cookie that opens the page, its badges and its subscription form for 30 days. Changing or removing the password closes the page again for every visitor. On a custom domain the path is `/api/public/status/unlock`. Limited to 10 wrong passwords per client address and 100 per page every 15 minutes.

**Access:** No authentication.

200.description: Unlocked (or the page has no password); the cookie is set.

path.description: Path in the JSON body: dot notation with [n] for array items, e.g. data.items[0].status.

value.description: Expected value. Not used by exists / not_exists; a number for gt/gte/lt/lte; a regular expression for matches.

Assertion.description: A rule on the JSON body of an http or keyword response.

target.description: What to check, depends on the type: an http(s) URL (http, keyword, mcp), host:port (tcp, IPv6 in brackets: [2001:db8::1]:443), a hostname or IP (ping, dns), a connection URL (postgres://, mysql://, redis://, mongodb://), a container name or id (docker), grpc[s]://host:port[/service], smtp[s]://host[:port]. Empty for push.

interval_sec.description: Seconds between checks, 10 to 86400 (push: expected period, up to 7 days). 0 = default (60, push 3600).

retries.description: Consecutive failures before a location counts as down, 1 to 10.

method.description: HTTP method for http/keyword (default GET). For mcp: the transport, auto, streamable or sse.

expected_status.description: Accepted HTTP status codes, e.g. "200-299" or "200,301". For mcp: the minimum number of tools.

keyword.description: keyword: text that must appear in the body. mcp: comma separated tool names that must be listed.

keyword_invert.description: keyword: fail when the text is found.

dns_record.description: dns: record type (A, AAAA, CNAME, MX, TXT, NS...).

dns_server.description: dns: resolver to query, host[:port]. Empty = system resolver.

dns_expected.description: dns: value that must be in the answer.

ip_family.description: 0 = instance default (GeneralSettings.ip_family), 1 = IPv4 or IPv6 (whichever connects first), 4 = IPv4 only, 6 = IPv6 only, 46 = IPv4 and IPv6 (both checked, the check fails when either fails). Locations without IPv6 check over IPv4 with 0 and 1; 6 and 46 are refused on them (see Location.ipv6). Ignored for push and docker.

assertions.description: JSON response rules, http and keyword only, at most 20.

grace_sec.description: push: extra time after the period before the monitor goes down, 0 to 86400.

degraded_pct.description: Share of failing locations (percent) from which the monitor is degraded, 1 to 50. 0 = instance default.

locations.description: Where the check runs: "local" (the hub) and/or "agent:<id>". Empty = local. See GET /api/locations.

cert_expiry_alert.description: Alert before the TLS certificate expires (https targets).

domain_expiry_alert.description: Alert before the domain registration expires.

paused.description: Create the monitor paused. Ignored on update: use POST /api/monitors/{id}/pause.

push_token.description: push: token of the heartbeat URL. Hidden from read-only users.

status_since.description: Unix time in milliseconds (0 = never / unknown).

created_at.description: Unix time in milliseconds (0 = never / unknown).

ts.description: Unix time in milliseconds (0 = never / unknown).

message.description: Error or detail of the check.

cert_expiry.description: TLS certificate expiry seen by this check.

timing.description: HTTP checks only, from the hub and agents that measure phases.

ok.description: Checks outside maintenance taken while the monitor was up or degraded. One failing location among several does not lower it.

degraded.description: Checks outside maintenance taken while the monitor was degraded.

expires_at.description: Unix time in milliseconds (0 = never / unknown).

checked_at.description: Unix time in milliseconds (0 = never / unknown).

uptime_24h.description: Share of checks taken while the monitor was up or degraded (not of single location checks), maintenance excluded. -1 without data.

end_at.description: Unix time in milliseconds (0 = never / unknown).

maintenance.description: Window covering the monitor right now.

uptime_7d.description: Share of checks taken while the monitor was up or degraded (not of single location checks), maintenance excluded. -1 without data.

uptime_30d.description: Share of checks taken while the monitor was up or degraded (not of single location checks), maintenance excluded. -1 without data.

t.description: Unix time in milliseconds (0 = never / unknown).

ok.description: Per location: checks that succeeded there. Otherwise: checks taken while the monitor was up or degraded.

degraded.description: Checks taken while the monitor was degraded (0 per location).

phases.description: Average per phase of the OK HTTP checks that measured it.

started_at.description: Unix time in milliseconds (0 = never / unknown).

monitors.description: Number of monitors in the group (read only).

created_at.description: Unix time in milliseconds (0 = never / unknown).

name.description: Unique, up to 32 characters, no commas.

created_at.description: Unix time in milliseconds (0 = never / unknown).

tag_ids.description: Every monitor with one of these tags.

start_at.description: once: start. Recurring: first day the schedule is valid (0 = now).

end_at.description: once: end. Recurring: last day the schedule is valid (0 = forever).

duration_min.description: Recurring: length in minutes, up to 7 days.

created_at.description: Unix time in milliseconds (0 = never / unknown).

active_end.description: Unix time in milliseconds (0 = never / unknown).

next_end.description: Unix time in milliseconds (0 = never / unknown).

last_seen.description: Unix time in milliseconds (0 = never / unknown).

created_at.description: Unix time in milliseconds (0 = never / unknown).

ipv6.description: IPv6 connectivity as last probed: 0 unknown (agents before this field), 1 available, 2 not available. IPv6-only monitors cannot use a location with 2, and monitors with ip_family 0 check over IPv4 there.

location_id.description: Value to use in monitor locations.

self_update.description: The agent can replace its own binary.

ipv6.description: IPv6 connectivity as last probed: 0 unknown (agents before this field), 1 available, 2 not available. IPv6-only monitors cannot use a location with 2, and monitors with ip_family 0 check over IPv4 there.

config.description: webhook, discord, slack, ntfy: {url}. telegram: {bot_token, chat_id}. email: {host, port, security (starttls|tls|none), username, password, from, to}. app: {users}, emails of the users whose phones get the alerts, comma separated (empty = every user). The email password is write-only: responses carry password_set="true" instead, and an empty password on update keeps the stored one. Read-only users see secrets as ********.

delay_min.description: Minutes a monitor must stay down before this channel gets its first alert (0 = right away). Use it for an escalation contact: shorter outages never reach it, and it gets the recovery message only if it was alerted.

repeat_min.description: Repeat the alert every this many minutes while the monitor stays down (0 = once, otherwise at least 5). Reminders carry reminder=1, 2, ... and down_since in the webhook payload. Nothing is sent during maintenance windows.

created_at.description: Unix time in milliseconds (0 = never / unknown).

slug.description: URL path: /status/<slug>. 1-50 lowercase letters, digits or dashes.

domain.description: Optional custom domain serving the page, e.g. status.example.com.

published.description: Drafts are visible only to logged-in users.

group_ids.description: Every monitor of these groups, current and future.

created_at.description: Unix time in milliseconds (0 = never / unknown).

subscribe_notifier_id.description: Email notification channel that sends incident updates to the page's subscribers (its SMTP server and sender are used, its recipients are not). 0 = visitors cannot subscribe.

protected.description: Visitors need a password to open the page, its badges and its subscription form. Logged-in users open it without one. On save, false removes the password and true keeps the current one.

password.description: New password for visitors (6-72 characters), stored hashed and never returned. Needed when protected is set on a page without one.

status.description: Overall state, from the monitors and the open incidents written on the page (minor impact = degraded, major = partial outage, critical = major outage), whichever is worse.

uptime.description: Over the shown days. Share of checks taken while the monitor was up or degraded (not of single location checks), maintenance excluded. -1 without data.

uptime_24h.description: Share of checks taken while the monitor was up or degraded (not of single location checks), maintenance excluded. -1 without data.

started_at.description: Unix time in milliseconds (0 = never / unknown).

resolved_at.description: Unix time in milliseconds (0 = never / unknown).

updated_at.description: Unix time in milliseconds (0 = never / unknown).

reports.description: Incidents written on the page: the open ones and those resolved in the shown days, open first.

subscribe.description: Visitors can subscribe to incident updates by email.

public_url.description: Public URL of the hub, used in links, agent setup and OAuth callbacks.

local_name.description: Name of the hub's own location.

ip_family.description: Default IP family of monitors with ip_family 0: 1 IPv4 or IPv6 (default), 4 IPv4 only, 6 IPv6 only, 46 IPv4 and IPv6. Locations without IPv6 check those monitors over IPv4.

disabled.description: Stop asking GitHub for new releases. PINGTXT_DISABLE_UPDATE_CHECK=true sets it on first start.

allow_signup.description: Create accounts on first single sign-on login.

allowed_domains.description: Email domains allowed to sign up, empty = any.

client_secret.description: Write-only: empty keeps the stored one.

detected_url.description: URL of the hub as seen in this request.

created_at.description: Unix time in milliseconds (0 = never / unknown).

staged_at.description: Unix time in milliseconds (0 = never / unknown).

ConfigDocument.description: Monitors, agents, notification channels, groups, tags, maintenance windows, status pages and settings, referenced by name. Export one with GET /api/config/export to see the full shape.

expires_at.description: Unix time in milliseconds (0 = never / unknown).

created_at.description: Unix time in milliseconds (0 = never / unknown).

last_used_at.description: Unix time in milliseconds (0 = never / unknown).

push_device.description: Name of the phone that gets push notifications through this sign-in, if any.

current.description: Version of this hub, e.g. v0.1.0 (dev or main-abc1234 for development and branch builds).

check_enabled.description: The hub looks for new releases: on in the settings and running a release build.

latest.description: Latest published release, null until the first check.

checked_at.description: Unix ms of the last check, 0 if none yet.

asked.description: An admin answered the opt-in question.

forced_off.description: PINGTXT_DISABLE_TELEMETRY is set or this is a development build.

report.description: Exactly what the next hourly report sends (null when off).

sent_at.description: Last report sent (unix ms), 0 if none yet.

weekly.description: Send a report every Monday for the week before.

monthly.description: Send a report on the 1st for the month before.

hour.description: Hour of the day the reports are sent, in `timezone`.

timezone.description: IANA time zone of the periods and of the times in the report.

notifier_ids.description: Email channels that receive the reports. Disabled channels are skipped.

group_ids.description: Only these monitor groups. Empty: every monitor.

next.description: When the next report of each enabled kind goes out (unix ms), by kind.

duration_ms.description: Part of the incident inside the period.

uptime.description: 0 to 1, -1 without data. Degraded counts as up, maintenance is left out.

prev_uptime.description: 0 to 1, -1 without data. Degraded counts as up, maintenance is left out.

uptime.description: Average uptime of the monitors of the group, -1 without data.

from.description: Start of the period (unix ms, included).

to.description: End of the period (unix ms, excluded).

uptime.description: Average uptime of the monitors, -1 without data.

text.description: Plain text body of the email.

url.description: Public URL of the hub, when set.

Phases.description: Time per phase of an HTTP check, in ms. With redirects the phases of every hop are added up; what is left of the latency is reading the response body.

ttfb_ms.description: Wait from the request being sent to the first byte of the response.

total_ms.description: Buckets only: average latency of the checks the phases come from.

n.description: Buckets only: how many checks the averages come from.

created_at.description: Unix time in milliseconds (0 = never / unknown).

PageIncident.description: An incident written on a status page, with its timeline of updates.

created_at.description: Unix time in milliseconds (0 = never / unknown).

updated_at.description: Unix time in milliseconds (0 = never / unknown).

resolved_at.description: When it was resolved, unix ms. 0 = still open.

title.description: One line, at most 200 characters. Required to create and to edit.

status.description: Status of the update. Default investigating when creating.

message.description: Text of the update, at most 5000 characters. Required to create and for updates.

notify.description: Email the update to the confirmed subscribers of the page (default true). Ignored when editing the title or impact.

confirmed_at.description: When the address confirmed, unix ms. 0 = waiting for confirmation.

created_at.description: Unix time in milliseconds (0 = never / unknown).

access_token.description: Bearer token for the API and /mcp (pma_...).

refresh_token.description: Single use (pmr_...): every refresh returns a new one.

enabled.description: Alerts can be sent to the mobile app.

relay_url.description: Base URL of the push relay.

hub_id.description: Id of this hub at the relay (public: the app sends it to the relay).

registered.description: The hub has a token from the relay. The token itself is never returned.

created_at.description: Unix time in milliseconds (0 = never / unknown).

last_seen_at.description: Unix time in milliseconds (0 = never / unknown).

skipped.description: The location could not run the check (offline or turned off); message says why.
